name: Leukocyte Adhesion Deficiency Type I

criteria.description: Deficiency or absence of CD18 integrin expression on leukocytes confirmed by flow cytometry
Recurrent severe bacterial infections without pus formation
Delayed separation of the umbilical cord beyond 3 weeks of age
Persistent peripheral blood neutrophilia during infections
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the ITGB2 gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent bacterial infections with delayed umbilical cord separation plus either CD18 deficiency on flow cytometry or pathogenic ITGB2 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by flow cytometric analysis of CD18 expression and/or genetic testing.

pathognomonic.notes: Umbilical cord separation delayed beyond 3 weeks

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent severe bacterial infections without pus formation
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic lack of purulence despite infection

pathognomonic.symptomName: Marked peripheral blood neutrophilia during infections

common.notes: Delayed or poor healing of skin wounds
Severe gum disease leading to early tooth loss

rare.notes: Painful ulcerations in the oral mucosa

laboratory: Flow cytometry showing absent or reduced CD18 expression on neutrophils
imaging: Radiographic evidence of osteomyelitis in complicated cases
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in ITGB2 gene encoding CD18 integrin
other: Absence of pus formation despite severe infections

distinguishingFeatures: Defect in NADPH oxidase causing impaired oxidative burst
Complement deficiency leading to recurrent infections

redFlags: Recurrent severe bacterial infections without pus formation
Delayed umbilical cord separation beyond 3 weeks
references: Etzioni A, et al. Leukocyte adhesion deficiency: a syndrome of defective leukocyte motility and recurrent infection. Immunol Today. 1992.
Almarza Novoa M, et al. Leukocyte adhesion deficiency type I: clinical presentation and molecular basis. J Clin Immunol. 2019.
